heading: Two walls, max water area
body:
Pick any two vertical lines from an array to form a container. The **area** is width × height:
- **Width**: distance between the two lines
- **Height**: the shorter wall (water overflows there)

Goal: find the max area in O(n) time.

heading: Always move the shorter wall
body:
Start pointers at both ends (widest container). Why move the shorter wall?

**Moving the taller wall can never help** because:
- Width decreases
- Height is still capped by the shorter wall

So we move the shorter wall, hoping to find a taller one.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we always move the pointer at the shorter wall?
options: Because the shorter wall determines the maximum height, and moving the taller wall can only decrease area
Because the taller wall should stay fixed to maximize height
Because we want to minimize the width as quickly as possible
Because the array must be sorted for two pointers to work
explain: Moving the taller wall inward decreases width while height remains capped by the shorter wall—this can never improve area.
